summary: Renewed geopolitical frictions in West Asia and supply chain disruptions have amplified inflationary pressures, prompting major central banks to raise policy rates. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies (AEs) have also brought into focus concerns about fiscal sustainability and its implications for financial stability. The Indian economy continued to demonstrate strength as evidenced by high-frequency indicators across both industry and services. The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation edged up in September driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel, and core components. Double-digit growth in merchandise exports during the first six months of 2026-27 helped in narrowing the trade deficit. FDI, ECB and remittance flows strengthened in August. Strong inflows under the FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves.
conclusion: Global economy is currently passing through a rough phase with multiple shocks. Although IMF has revised upwards the global economic outlook for 2026 and 2027, the prospect remains clouded by significant downside risks. Rising inflationary pressures induced by West Asia crisis and recurrent trade tensions, alongside multi-decade-high sovereign bond yields, elevated public debt, and broader fiscal sustainability concerns are looming large. Some silver linings are evident in the form of positive technology shocks and related dividends from AI. Navigating this environment, the Indian economy has been anchored by solid macroeconomic fundamentals and policy interventions to cushion downside risks. Despite being a net energy importer, GDP growth has been supported by sustained domestic demand and services. Headline CPI inflation edged up over the months and showed signs of greater generalisation across commodities calling for a commensurate change in the monetary policy stance. The external headwinds are also being dealt with a slew of regulatory measures by the Reserve Bank to curb speculative activity in foreign exchange market. Strong inflows under FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves. FDI, ECB and remittance flows strengthened in August. With strong exports growth, the trade deficit narrowed in September.

changes.now: The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5 per cent (y-o-y) in September from 4.8 per cent in August, driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel and core (CPI excluding food and fuel) components.
changes.before: Headline CPI inflation increased to 4.8 per cent (y-o-y) in August from 4.5 per cent in July 2026, driven by food and beverages and a pickup in fuel and core components (CPI inflation excluding food and fuel).

changes.now: Economic activity remained robust in September as indicated by several high-frequency indicators.
changes.before: Despite geopolitical uncertainties, Indian economy clocked a growth of 7.8 per cent in Q1:2026-27 driven by domestic consumption and investment.

changes.now: The south-west monsoon season (June-September) ended with rainfall of 87 per cent of the long period average (LPA) with uneven spatial and temporal distribution.
changes.before: The real gross value added (GVA) grew by 8.2 per cent in Q1:2026-27 supported by strong manufacturing and services activity.

changes.now: System liquidity remained in surplus during September and early October supported by strong inflows under FCNR(B) swap facility.
changes.before: System liquidity remained in surplus in August and surged further in September (till 21st), amidst strong inflows under the FCNR(B) swap facility.

changes.now: Despite confronting a series of shocks during the year, the global economy held up well.
changes.before: Global uncertainty increased during August and September (till 21st) amidst renewed geopolitical tensions, heightened trade policy risks, and concerns over global economic prospects.
